_uwaga: Procedury awaryjne wyświetlane w zakładce EMERGENCY (kolejność = kolejność w menu). Punkt to tekst albo {"text": ..., "items": [...]} (podpunkty) albo {"note": ...} (akapit). "assist": true pokazuje nad procedurą przypomnienie ASSIST. Checklisty 16 scenariuszy pochodzą z EUROCONTROL HRS/TSP-004-GUI-05 (Annex B) – tekst oryginalny, po angielsku.

items: Make sure you understood the nature of emergency and acknowledge accordingly.
Impose silence on your control frequency if necessary.
Don't disturb urgent cockpit actions by unnecessary transmissions!
Inform your supervisor and other sectors/units concerned.
Give maximum support to pilot and crew.
Allow pilots sufficient time to work on their problem.

sections.title: ACC / APP / TWR
items: Consider airspace boundaries / coordinate a short-cut
Check aircraft status / crew intentions (diversion, injuries, aircraft damage)
Assume the a/c is still in distress
If necessary, broadcast the descent on the ATC frequency and the emergency frequency

sections.title: Additional information:
items: Time until the descent starts is 5 to 15 seconds on average (initial rate of descent 7000 ft/min to 14000 ft/min)
Squawk 7700 appears late or not at all

ATC is usually informed too late because of the crew's limited capacity to act; when oxygen masks are put on, reception switches automatically from the headsets to the cockpit loudspeaker, so the cockpit microphone and communication may be disturbed by background noise
Because of the rapid loss of cabin pressure, gas pressure in the human body rises and the crew feel unwell
Time until the crew (without oxygen) lose consciousness is 4 to 30 seconds depending on the flight level (time of useful consciousness)

procedures.label: ACAS/TCAS
procedures.title: ACAS / TCAS
procedures.source: EUROCONTROL, Guidelines for Controller Training in the Handling of Unusual/Emergency Situations (HRS/TSP-004-GUI-05, ed. 2.0), Annex B

sections.title: Expect
items: Climb or descent without prior warning
Notification from pilot of 'TCAS climb' or 'TCAS descent'

sections.title: Remember

items.text: When a pilot reports a manoeuvre induced by an RA:
items: the controller shall not attempt to modify the aircraft flight path
the controller shall provide traffic information as appropriate
TCAS II altitude data is more accurate than radar data

items.note: NB: Once an aircraft departs from its clearance in compliance with a RA, the controller ceases to be responsible for providing separation between that aircraft and any other aircraft affected as a direct consequence of the manoeuvre induced by the RA.

items.text: The controller shall resume responsibility for providing separation for all the affected aircraft when:
items: 1. The controller acknowledges a report from the flight crew that the aircraft has resumed the current clearance, OR
2. The controller acknowledges a report from the flight crew that the aircraft is resuming the current clearance and issues an alternative clearance which is acknowledged by the flight crew.
Following an RA event, or other significant ACAS event, pilots and controllers should complete an air traffic incident report

items: Report arrival by the most expeditious means to the appropriate ATS unit
Maintain last assigned speed and level for 7 mins OR minimum flight altitude, if the minimum flight altitude is higher than the last assigned level
No compulsory reporting points OR position reports omitted: at the time the last assigned level or minimum flight altitude is reached, OR at the time of squawk 7600, whichever is LATER

Compulsory reporting points AND position reports not omitted: at the time the last assigned level or minimum flight altitude is reached, OR at the previously reported pilot estimate for the compulsory reporting point, OR at the time of a failed report over a compulsory reporting point, whichever is LATER
Thereafter, comply with the filed flight plan

If being radar vectored, or proceeding offset according to RNAV without a specified limit, proceed in the most direct manner possible to rejoin the CPL no later than the next significant point, taking into consideration the applicable min. flight altitude
The ACFT will proceed to the designated navigational aid serving the destination aerodrome and hold until commencement of descent

Commence descent at, or as close as possible to, the EAT last received and acknowledged, OR if no EAT received and acknowledged, commence descent at, or as close as possible to, the ETA resulting from the CPL
Complete a normal instrument approach procedure as specified for the designated navigation aid
Land, if possible, within 30 minutes after the ETA specified, OR within 30 minutes of the last acknowledged expected approach time, whichever is later

procedures.label: DESCENT
procedures.title: Emergency Descent
procedures.source: EUROCONTROL, Guidelines for Controller Training in the Handling of Unusual/Emergency Situations (HRS/TSP-004-GUI-05, ed. 2.0), Annex B

items.text: When an aircraft operated as a controlled flight experiences sudden decompression or a (similar) malfunction requiring an emergency descent, the aircraft shall, if able:
items: Initiate a turn away from the assigned route or track before commencing the emergency descent
Advise the appropriate air traffic control unit as soon as possible of the emergency descent
Set transponder to Code 7700 and select the Emergency Mode on ADS/CPDLC system, if applicable
Watch for conflicting traffic both visually and by reference to ACAS (if equipped)
Coordinate its further intentions with the appropriate ATC unit

items.note: The aircraft shall not descend below the lowest published minimum altitude which will provide a minimum vertical clearance of 300 m (1000 ft) or in designated mountainous terrain 600 m (2000 ft) above all obstacles located in the area specified.

sections.title: Remember
items: Take all necessary action to safeguard all aircraft concerned
May be required to suggest a heading
May be required to state the minimum altitude
Provide separation or issue essential traffic information, as appropriate
Consider ACFT still to be in an emergency situation
